 Live .  44,692 viewing 44692 viewing Live page Updated 7 minutes ago Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond, ending long hunt for Daniel Craig's replacement
 New James Bond Actor Revealed As Robert Pattinson
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Robert Pattinson has been named as the new James Bond - here's an image of the actor in the role, released on social media 
 In a statement, the 40-year-old British actor says "to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime"
 Pattinson will become only the seventh person to play the secret agent in the official film series - it's one of the biggest roles in cinema, writes our entertainment correspondent 
 Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight has been writing the script for the next film, with Dune's Denis Villeneuve to direct - what we do, and don't, know about the film 
 Speculation about Daniel Craig's replacement has been rife, with actors including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden thought to have made it to the final screen tests
 Thanking those who auditioned, Villeneuve says "we were surrounded by extraordinary talent", adding Pattinson "brings a spirit that is completely new"
 Close form Share your reaction
 Get in touch Media caption, Watch: Footage from 2010 shows Pattinson being asked about playing Bond Live Reporting
 Edited by Kieran Kelly and Caitlin Doherty
 Pattinson's career through the years - in pictures published at 16:28 GMT 16:28 GMT 
 Robert Pattinson has played a huge range of characters: an immortal being in Twilight, Batman, controversial TV presenter Chris Hansen, and many other notable roles. 
 Here's a look at Pattinson's career in pictures:

 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Pattinson is also the latest actor to play Batman, starring in the role for the first time in 2022
 Image source, PA Media Image caption, Pattinson recently starred in Christopher Nolan's Odyssey as Antinous

 Bond reveal comes 20 years after release of Casino Royale published at 16:15 GMT 16:15 GMT 
 Today's reveal comes 20 years after the release of Casino Royale - Daniel Craig's first film starring as 007.
 The 21st official Bond film had its world premiere on 14 November 2006 in London, and was then subsequently released in UK cinemas on 16 November.
 Craig played the role in five Bond films spanning 15 years.
 Media caption, Watch: What Daniel Craig said when he was cast as Bond in 2005

 What we do and don't know about the next Bond film published at 16:11 GMT 16:11 GMT 
 The next James Bond actor has finally been unveiled as Robert Pattinson - here's everything else we do and don't know about the next 007 film:
 We do know...
 The writer and director: Steven Knight will pen the script, while Denis Villeneuve will direct the film
 A rough date: the film is expected to go into production in 2027, before its release in 2028
 It will be the 26th film in the official series
 We still don't know...
 The name of the next film
 Its exact release date
 Which artist will be chosen to perform the Bond theme and title song
 Other actors in the cast, such as the villain

 New era of Bond unveiled on social media published at 16:05 GMT 16:05 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Robert Pattinson was revealed as 007 in a slick social media post featuring the actor dressed in a black tuxedo.
 A short video also shows the actor pointing a gun as he is surrounded by darkness.
 The words "James Bond will return" then follow.
 The announcement could not be more different to when Daniel Craig was revealed as the sixth Bond actor back in 2005.
 Craig arrived at a news conference in London on a Royal Marines speedboat, joking that he "had a couple of Martinis" after securing the role.

 Robert Pattinson is a bankable movie star published at 15:55 GMT 15:55 GMT 
 Steven McIntosh 
Entertainment reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images One of the most interesting things about the choice of Robert Pattinson to play 007 is that he is an actor who already has significant profile.
 Many of the other contenders thought to have been in the race - such as Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor - might all be hot, up-and-coming actors, but none is truly a household name. 
 Pattinson, on the other hand, is a proper movie star, with a proven track record of box office success and ability to lead major franchises such as Twilight and The Batman. 
 Whatever your opinion on Pattinson, one thing for sure is that most will have at least heard of him. 
 Daniel Craig might not have been an A-lister when he was cast as Bond, but this time producers clearly wanted a bankable name to lead the first iteration of Bond under Amazon's umbrella.

 Pattinson's appeal with younger fans will please producers published at 15:47 GMT 15:47 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Robert Pattinson took over as Batman in 2022
 This choice will please a lot of millennial and Gen Z fans.
 Robert Pattinson – or R-Patz, as many refer to him – became something of a pin-up after playing vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight series, alongside American actress Kristen Stewart.
 Before that, he stole young hearts as Hufflepuff hunk Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.
 His more recent choice of films have also positioned him well to win over the youth market – from Dune: Part Three, to The Batman.
 That will no doubt have been appealing for producers, who will be looking to bring in newer Bond fans to the franchise.

 'Legacy of this character is in great hands', say producers published at 15:40 GMT 15:40 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Amy Pascal and David Heyman, two heavyweight producers behind the next James Bond movie, say the "legacy of this character is in great hands" with Robert Pattinson.
 In a joint statement, the pair say: "James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic, and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies. 
 "The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. 
 "His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times."
 Pascal has produced movies including Ghostbusters, Little Women and Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, winning a Golden Globe award for the latter in 2019.
 Heyman has been working in the film industry since 1992 and has won 12 awards, the majority of them for his work on the Harry Potter and Paddington franchises.

 Only six people have ever played Bond - one of the biggest roles in cinema published at 15:25 GMT 15:25 GMT 
 Lizo Mzimba 
Entertainment correspondent 
 People have been talking about this moment for five years, ever since Daniel Craig said he would not be returning to the role for the next Bond film.
 It's one of the biggest roles in cinema.
 Only six people have ever played Bond in the official series. It will be seven when Pattinson starts. 
 Twice as many people as have walked on the Moon. That's how special this job is.

 Pattinson has the 'timeless soul of 007', says director Denis Villeneuve published at 15:16 GMT 15:16 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images We've also been hearing from the next James Bond film's director Denis Villeneuve.
 He says in a statement: "Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. 
 "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007.
 "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. 
 "He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin."

 Pattinson says playing Bond is the 'honour of a lifetime' published at 15:10 GMT 15:10 GMT Breaking 
 In a statement, Pattinson says: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime.
 "I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. 
 "I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team."

 Robert Pattinson confirmed as new James Bond published at 15:00 GMT 15:00 GMT Breaking
